headline: ELEVRA LOCKS IN LG ENERGY SOLUTION — 240,000-TONNE SPODUMENE DEAL FROM QUEBEC'S NAL MINE RUNS THROUGH 2029
snippet: Elevra Lithium Limited (ASX: EVR) executed a binding spodumene concentrate supply agreement with South Korea's LG Energy Solution for 240,000 dry metric tonnes from its North American Lithium (NAL) operation in Québec, with deliveries running 2026 through 2029 at market-linked pricing tied to lithium content. An optional tranche of up to 90,000 dmt brings maximum volume to 330,000 dmt. The deal positions NAL — one of the few operating hard-rock lithium mines in North America — as a direct feedstock supplier for LG's EV battery gigafactories.

headline: NORTHWEST COPPER KWANIKA WESTERN ZONE DELIVERS — 108.7M AT 0.70% CU, 1.69 G/T AU (2.53% CUEQ) FROM 352M
snippet: NorthWest Copper Corp. (TSXV: NWST) intersected 108.7 metres of 0.70% copper and 1.69 g/t gold (2.53% copper equivalent) in the Western Zone at its Kwanika Copper-Gold Project in central British Columbia, starting at 352.8 metres depth. The result extends the higher-grade corridor targeted by the company's 2026 target model, which outlines Pit, Central and Western zones grading 1.5–2.5% CuEq. An updated mineral resource and new PEA are expected by year-end — each Western Zone intercept directly informs those studies.

headline: FIRST MAJESTIC Q3 OUT — 3.4M OZ SILVER, 29,552 OZ GOLD DESPITE 12-DAY SAN DIMAS STRIKE; SILVER-EQUIVALENT OUTPUT +39% YOY
snippet: First Majestic Silver Corp. (TSX: AG) reported Q3 2026 production of approximately 3.4 million ounces of silver and 29,552 ounces of gold — with a 12-day labour dispute at San Dimas curtailing output below run-rate — while silver-equivalent production across the consolidated portfolio rose 39% year-over-year. The company also renewed its share buyback program and announced a conference call for Q3 financial results. With silver still below $60 per ounce, all-in sustaining costs per silver-equivalent ounce will be the key number for investors watching margin compression.

headline: GOLD RECLAIMS $4,150 AS OCTOBER RATE HIKE ODDS DROP TO 22% — $4,100 FLOOR HOLDS AFTER THREE-WEEK SELLOFF
snippet: Gold recovered to $4,152 per ounce on October 8 as weaker-than-expected September U.S. payrolls sharply reduced the probability of a Federal Reserve rate hike at the October 28 FOMC meeting — with CME FedWatch pricing now putting odds of no hike above 78%. The $4,100–4,086 support area absorbed three weeks of selling pressure from above $4,500; with rate-hike fears receding, the next test is whether gold can reclaim the $4,300 level before year-end. Silver remained below $60 at $58.94, still down 12% from its September peak.

headline: K2 GOLD EXTENDS DRAGONFLY, ADDS FLORES AS SECOND HIGH-GRADE TARGET — MOJAVE CAMPAIGN WIDENS BEYOND SINGLE ZONE
snippet: K2 Gold Corp. (TSXV: KTO) extended the Dragonfly Zone at its Mojave Project in Inyo County, California with new drill holes — the program has previously returned 6.68 g/t gold over 45.72 metres from surface — and identified the Flores Target as an additional high-grade area with surface rock samples grading up to 10.9 g/t gold. The Dragonfly extension and Flores identification expand Mojave from a single-zone story into a multi-target system within the existing fully permitted plan-of-operations boundary, with 14,000 metres permitted and the 2026 campaign still advancing.

headline: EQUITY METALS SILVER QUEEN VALIDATION: 661 G/T AGEQ OVER 2.6M — 5,719 METRES CONFIRMS NO. 3 VEIN CONTINUITY IN BC
snippet: Equity Metals Corporation (TSXV: EQTY) released assays from 17 validation holes totaling 5,719 metres at the Silver Queen Gold-Silver Project in northern British Columbia, highlighted by 2.6 metres (estimated true width) of 661 g/t silver equivalent on the No. 3 Vein. The validation program is specifically designed to confirm historical drill grades ahead of an economic assessment — hole-by-hole verification of Silver Queen's high-grade vein resource materially lowers the technical risk discount that has historically held back project valuation in the Omineca Mining Division.

headline: GOOGLE LOCKS IN 3,590 MW CONSTELLATION NUCLEAR DEAL — $4.3B IN REACTOR UPGRADES SENDS URANIUM STOCKS UP 3–5%
snippet: Constellation Energy (Nasdaq: CEG) shares surged 14% after Google signed agreements to purchase 3,590 megawatts of nuclear power: a 20-year deal for 890 MW from uprates at 11 existing reactors, plus a 15-year contract for 2,700 MW from existing capacity, with $4.3 billion in upgrades and first new capacity by 2028. Uranium producers including Cameco (CCO), NexGen (NXE), and Uranium Energy (UEC) each gained 3–5% as the market read the deal as structural demand confirmation — reinforcing the Big Tech nuclear thesis that has kept uranium above $90/lb through October's broader commodity correction.

headline: WORKSAFE PUTS TALISON GREENBUSHES ON NOTICE — WORLD'S BIGGEST LITHIUM MINE FACES PROBE OVER WORKER PSYCHOLOGICAL DISTRESS
snippet: Western Australia's WorkSafe authority issued a formal notice to Talison Lithium after finding evidence of psychological distress among workers at the Greenbushes Lithium Mine — the world's largest hard-rock lithium operation, owned 60% by Albemarle and 40% by Tianqi. The finding follows a pattern of safety concerns linked to the mine's multi-billion-dollar expansion, with workers previously raising concerns about inadequate safeguards on site. The investigation adds regulatory and reputational risk to a project that supplies spodumene concentrate to battery manufacturers globally.

headline: RUA GOLD ANTIMONY PROJECT FAST-TRACKED — NZ APPLICATION DUE IN WEEKS, PFS TARGETED DECEMBER ON WORLD-CLASS ANTIMONY RESOURCE
snippet: RUA GOLD Inc. (TSX: RUA) is targeting a substantive Fast-Track Approvals application in October 2026 for its Reefton Gold-Antimony Project in New Zealand — one of the world's largest antimony resources — following its listing under the NZ government's Fast-Track regime in July. With 19,600 metres of drilling complete and a pre-feasibility study due in December 2026, the project builds on a May 2026 PEA showing a US$42M after-tax NPV at US$132.6M initial capex. Antimony is trading at record prices as a critical input for military ordnance, flame retardants, and battery technology.

headline: TANBREEZ GREENBUSHES ENVIRONMENT PLAN APPROVED — GREENLAND'S $3B NPV RARE EARTH GIANT TARGETS Q4 FEASIBILITY SUBMISSION
snippet: Critical Metals Corp. (Nasdaq: CRML) received Greenland government approval for the Tanbreez Mine's geochemical test work and closure plan from the Environment Agency for Mineral Resource Activities (EAMRA), clearing a permitting milestone for one of the world's largest rare earth deposits in southern Greenland. The feasibility study is 70% complete with a Q4 2026 submission targeted; the PEA calculated a US$3 billion after-tax NPV. With Western governments prioritising non-Chinese rare earth supply, Tanbreez's 45-million-tonne resource and Greenland's stable permitting framework position it as a strategic alternative to Chinese-controlled deposits.

headline: ALASKA SILVER SETS DEPTH RECORD AT ILLINOIS CREEK — 1,288M DEEP HOLE COMPLETES 2026 PROGRAM, ASSAYS PENDING
snippet: Alaska Silver Metals Inc. (TSXV: WAM) completed its 2026 summer drill program at the Illinois Creek Gold-Silver Project in central Alaska, achieving the deepest hole ever drilled at the property at 1,288.24 metres — the capstone of a fully funded 6,000-metre campaign split across the Waterpump Creek South and Silver Sage zones. All assay results are pending; earlier holes in the program tested the down-plunge extension of the gold-silver system, and the depth record signals the company is now chasing a vertical dimension to the deposit that was not explored in the 2025 program.
